title: Asset metadata
description: The metadata every selectable object carries, in every module, in every viewer mode. This is what the shared metadata panel renders. Module-specific fields live under 'extensions' keyed by module_id so neither team can break the other's panel.

local_id.description: The module's own identifier, e.g. a part_id or a BIN. Must equal the suffix of asset_id.

category.description: Coarse class shared by both modules. Fine-grained taxonomy stays module-local under 'taxonomy'.

taxonomy.description: Module-local classification. The bridge uses system/subsystem; the district uses land use and building class.

path.description: Hierarchical path for tree widgets, e.g. ['towers','manhattan'] or ['buildings','warehouse'].

source_refs.description: Source register IDs this asset's geometry consumed.

basis_confidence.description: Grade of this asset's own basis, before the weakest-link rule is applied against its control references.

control_refs.description: Control value IDs consumed, e.g. 'CTL-005' or 'DCTL-003'. Makes the weakest-link rule auditable.

open_questions.description: Unresolved question IDs. Every grade D asset MUST name at least one.

last_modified_by.description: Script or agent identifier plus version.

units.description: All shared metadata lengths are prototype meters. Display scales such as HO are a viewer concern, not a data concern.

anchor.description: Representative point used by tours for 'look at this' and by the map view for pin placement.

attributes.description: Free-form displayable facts, rendered as a key/value table. Values must be primitives so any viewer can render them without module-specific code.

extensions.description: Module-private payloads, keyed by module_id. A viewer MUST ignore extensions it does not recognise.
